steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), keeping the filter minimal so DESeq2's independent filtering does the rest. Set the condition factor's reference level explicitly to the control level as named in metadata.csv, so the contrast is condition, numerator = treated, denominator = control, and a positive log2FoldChange means higher in treated. Fit DESeq2 with design ~ condition, letting median-of-ratios size factors act as the offset inside the model (no pre-scaling of counts). Run the Wald test, extract results with alpha = 0.05, BH adjustment and independent filtering on. Keep the default Cook's-distance outlier behaviour: with 3 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags outlier genes and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts — count these genes and report them separately from genes dropped by the independent filter. Shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm on the treated-vs-control coefficient, keeping both the unshrunken and shrunken estimates plus lfcSE in the output table. Save the p-value histogram of the unadjusted p-values. Then, on the same filtered count matrix, run an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (TMM normalization, glmQLFit/glmQLFTest, BH at 0.05) as the independent second method and save its results table. Finally compute the expected power of this design in closed form — RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so write out the sample-size/power relation from sequencing depth, biological coefficient of variation (take the BCV from the edgeR common/trend dispersion estimated on this dataset), fold change, and alpha — and report the fold change detectable at 80% power at typical expression levels. Emit: the full DESeq2 results table (all tested genes, with baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj), the significant subset at padj < 0.05, the edgeR results table, and the power figures.

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with 3v3 power assessment
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level raw count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 6 sample columns plus the gene-symbol column) with a 6-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, one batch. The research question has two halves — which genes differ, and how much confidence three replicates per group buy — so the plan is one track of three steps that keeps both in view.

T1S1 runs the sample-structure QC that must precede any test on a 3v3 design: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes. With three samples per group a single mis-grouping sample or a depth outlier can create or destroy the entire result, so this step is diagnostic, not decorative, and it reports whether the samples separate by condition at all.

T1S2 fits the primary model. Counts stay raw into DESeq2 (median-of-ratios size factors act as an offset inside the negative binomial model; no pre-scaling), a minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=3 samples is applied, the condition factor gets an explicit reference level so the contrast is unambiguously treated over control, the Wald test runs at alpha 0.05 with BH and independent filtering, and apeglm shrinks the reported log2 fold changes. The same step runs an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the identical filtered matrix as the robustness second method, because at three replicates the two count models agree on most but not all genes and the intersection is the defensible high-confidence set. The step also computes the expected power of this design in closed form (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so the calculation is written out from depth, biological coefficient of variation, fold change, and alpha) and states the fold change detectable at 80% power.

T1S3 assembles the report: MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, gene tables carrying unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, the count of NA p-values split into outlier-flagged versus independent-filter-removed, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, and the power statement placed before the gene tables. The honest framing is fixed in advance: at n=3 per group these models recover only a minority of true differences, mostly large-fold-change ones, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change, and the threshold is not loosened to compensate.

No enrichment step is planned — the research question asks for differentially expressed genes and confidence, not pathways, and adding gene-set testing on a 3v3 result would be unasked scope on top of an underpowered list.

edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method
Report with power statement, MA and dispersion plots, method overlap, session info
